title: Resources
intro:
This tab lists the outside material that fits this plan, and only material that was checked on 2026-10-07.
Use it for three things: company facts before an exam, extra practice when a pattern feels weak, and setup help for Colab and the data files.
The plan itself is enough for most days. Outside practice is an addition, not a second plan.
Pages marked **(browser)** block scripted checks but open normally in a browser. **(login)** and **(Premium)** mean that a feature needs an account or a paid plan.

sections.title: How to use the handbook, the notebooks and outside practice
sections.summary: One plan, one mistake log, and a small, controlled amount of outside practice.
sections.body:
### The three layers
| Layer | What it is | When you use it |
|---|---|---|
| Daily notebooks | `exam_prep/day_NN/` with 4 exams: algorithms, SQL, stats, AI | Every day, first. This is the core work (about 2h15) |
| Handbook | The tabs of this website: patterns, templates, examples, cheat sheets | After a hint or a wrong answer: read the linked section, then retry |
| Outside practice | LeetCode lists, DataLemur, HI, books and courses below | Only to close a gap that the mistake log shows |

### A normal day
1. Warm-up (10 min): redo one item from the mistake log that is due (3 or 7 days old).
2. Algorithms notebook (50 to 55 min). Time boxes: 15 min stuck, open Hint 1. 25 min, open Hint 2 or the solution. Then log it.
3. SQL, stats and AI notebooks (20 to 25 min each).
4. Theory flashcards (10 min). Answer out loud before you reveal.
5. For every miss, open the `Learn more` link and read only that section. Do not read the whole tab.

### When to add outside practice
Add it only when one of these is true:
- The same pattern appears in your mistake log 2 or more times. Do 2 or 3 extra problems of that pattern from the [HI pattern pages](#resources-coding) or NeetCode, then stop.
- You have an exam date with a specific company. In the last 7 to 10 days, add 1 or 2 company-tagged problems per day (see [Companies](#resources-companies)).
- A whole area feels slow. For SQL, add 2 DataLemur questions a day (see [SQL practice](#resources-sql)). For A/B testing, read one article from [Statistics and product](#resources-stats-product).

### When to use LeetCode company lists
- Not in days 1 to 10. Company lists mix all patterns and difficulties. Early on they slow you down and hurt confidence.
- Days 11 to 20: only problems from the [frequent problems table](#resources-frequent-problems) whose pattern you have already met in the plan.
- Days 21 to 28: if you know your target company, use its tag list (or the free GitHub mirror) sorted by frequency. Do problems from the last 6 months first.
- Days 29 and 30: no new problems. Redo the mistake log.

### When to stop
Stop adding outside problems when any of these is true:
- You can recognize the pattern in under 2 minutes and solve a medium in about 25 minutes, with complexity, for most patterns in the [pattern recognition guide](#algo-recognize).
- Your daily load goes above about 3 hours. Fatigue costs more than one extra problem gives.
- You are 2 days before the exam. Then switch to the mistake log, [exam-day checklist](#cheat-exam-day) and behavioral stories.

Rough limits: at most 30 extra minutes per day, and at most about 40 to 60 extra algorithm problems over the 30 days. Redoing an old mistake is usually worth more than a new problem.

### One mistake log
Keep all mistakes, from the notebooks and from outside practice, in one log. For each item write: the problem, the signal you missed, the right pattern, and the next review dates (3 and 7 days later).

sections.title: Companies: TikTok/ByteDance, Google, Samsung, Meta, Amazon
sections.summary: What each company's data science loop usually contains, and the best links for each.
sections.body:
Exam loops change by team, level, country and year. Everything below is based on public guides and candidate reports, not on official documents, unless it says "official". Ask your recruiter for the exact rounds. That is the most reliable source and it is normal to ask.

### Common shape (most big-tech DS loops)
| Stage | Typical content |
|---|---|
| Recruiter call | Background, role fit, sometimes basic stats or SQL questions |
| Online assessment or technical screen | SQL and/or Python coding, sometimes a probability or stats question |
| Onsite or virtual onsite (3 to 5 rounds) | SQL / data manipulation, statistics and A/B testing, product sense or a metric case, ML (more for ML-heavy roles), behavioral |

The weight depends on the role. A **product / analytics DS** gets more SQL, A/B testing and product cases. An **ML / algorithm DS** gets more LeetCode-style coding and ML system design.

### TikTok / ByteDance
- **Usually reported:** a coding round with LeetCode-style problems (often medium, sometimes hard), SQL, statistics and A/B testing, a product case about engagement, creators or recommendations, and ML questions for ML-leaning roles. Some candidates report an online assessment first.
- **Uncertain:** the number of rounds and whether a LeetCode round is used for product DS roles. Reports differ by team.
- TikTok is a frequent LeetCode tag: LRU Cache, Number of Islands and Longest Increasing Subsequence are its top 3.
- Links:
  - [DataLemur: TikTok DS exam guide](https://datalemur.com/blog/tiktok-data-scientist-interview-guide) (process and 22 reported questions)
  - [DataLemur: TikTok SQL questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/tiktok-sql-interview-questions)
  - [IQ: TikTok DS guide](https://www.interviewquery.com/guides/tiktok-data-scientist) and [ByteDance DS guide](https://www.interviewquery.com/guides/bytedance-data-scientist)
  - [HI: TikTok community questions](https://www.hellointerview.com/community/questions/company/TikTok) (part of the feed is Premium)
  - LeetCode tags: [TikTok](https://leetcode.com/company/tiktok/) and [ByteDance](https://leetcode.com/company/bytedance/) (browser, Premium for frequency)
  - Experience posts: [TikTok full virtual onsite](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/4377581/Tiktok-VO-Full-Loop/) and [TikTok online assessment](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/2729466/TikTok-OA-questions-(Latest)/) (browser; single reports, not a rule)
  - ML system design practice that matches the product: [video recommendations](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/ml-system-design/problem-breakdowns/video-recommendations)

### Google
- **Usually reported:** statistics and probability in depth, coding for data work (SQL or Python, sometimes a simple algorithm), a product or case question, and a behavioral round ("Googleyness" and leadership). Product Analytics roles focus on metrics and experiments.
- **Uncertain:** how much algorithm coding a DS candidate gets. It varies by role title and team.
- Links:
  - [IQ: Google DS guide](https://www.interviewquery.com/guides/google-data-scientist)
  - [DataLemur: Google SQL questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/google-sql-interview-questions)
  - [HI: Google community questions](https://www.hellointerview.com/community/questions/company/Google)
  - [LeetCode Google tag](https://leetcode.com/company/google/) (browser, Premium)
  - [Udacity A/B Testing](https://www.udacity.com/course/ab-testing--ud257) (a free course taught by Google data scientists)
  - [Google: Rules of ML](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml)

### Samsung
Samsung has very different tracks, so first find out which test you will take.
- **SW Competency Test (official, Samsung Careers):** coding on a PC, **2 problems in 240 minutes**, in C, C++, Java or Python. It is implementation-heavy: grid simulation (robots, snakes, dice, marbles, sharks), BFS/DFS on 2-D boards, brute force with backtracking, and rotating or shifting 2-D arrays. The difficulty is getting many rules exactly right, not advanced algorithms.
- **Python may be restricted** in some environments (for example, no `sys`). Check this before the test.
- **Other tracks (less certain):** DS and AI roles at Samsung Research or Samsung SDS may use the GSAT aptitude test plus a separate coding round. Samsung R&D India is reported to use a 3-question online test, then a 3-hour advanced test.
- How to train for the SW test: read the problem twice, write the rules as a numbered list, simulate on paper, then code one function per rule. Test with the given examples and with edge cases (walls, empty cells, ties). See [Grid simulation](#algo-grid-simulation) and [BFS and DFS](#algo-graphs-bfs-dfs).
- Links:
  - [Samsung Careers: recruiting process](https://www.samsungcareers.com/guide/process?lang=en) (official description of the SW test and GSAT)
  - [SW Expert Academy](https://swexpertacademy.com/main/main.do) and its [problem list](https://swexpertacademy.com/main/code/problem/problemList.do) (official practice; free with an account, login needed to submit). The mock SW competency test set (모의 SW 역량테스트) is the closest to the real exam
  - [CodeTree](https://www.codetree.ai/) (hosts recreations of past Samsung SW test problems; partly paid)
  - [Solutions repo for A-type past problems](https://github.com/bloodstrawberry/Samsung_Software_Competency_Test_A_Type) (shows the expected simulation style)
  - [IQ: Samsung DS guide](https://www.interviewquery.com/guides/samsung-data-scientist) and [DataLemur: Samsung SQL questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/samsung-sql-interview-questions)
  - [LeetCode Samsung tag](https://leetcode.com/company/samsung/) (browser, Premium). Used mainly by Samsung R&D India. Only 62 problems, so its ranking is noisy. It is not the Korean SW test
- **Baekjoon note:** Baekjoon Online Judge, the usual home of the past-problem list, shut down on 2026-04-28 and its pages did not load during checking, so it is not linked. Search for the classic problem names on CodeTree instead: 구슬 탈출 2, 2048 (Easy), 뱀, 주사위 굴리기, 테트로미노, 연구소, 로봇 청소기, 톱니바퀴, 감시, 치킨 배달, 아기 상어, 미세먼지 안녕!
- LeetCode problems that train the same skills: [Number of Islands](https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-islands/), [Rotting Oranges](https://leetcode.com/problems/rotting-oranges/), [Shortest Path in Binary Matrix](https://leetcode.com/problems/shortest-path-in-binary-matrix/), [Spiral Matrix](https://leetcode.com/problems/spiral-matrix/), [Word Search](https://leetcode.com/problems/word-search/), [N-Queens](https://leetcode.com/problems/n-queens/), [Making A Large Island](https://leetcode.com/problems/making-a-large-island/), [Number of Distinct Islands](https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-distinct-islands/).

### Meta (reference)
- **Usually reported for product DS:** a technical screen with SQL and a product question, then onsite rounds called analytical execution (stats, metrics, experiment analysis), analytical reasoning (product sense), technical (SQL) and behavioral. This loop is a good template for any product DS exam.
- Links: [DataLemur: Meta DS exam guide](https://datalemur.com/blog/meta-data-scientist-interview-guide), [DataLemur: Meta SQL questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/facebook-sql-interview-questions), [IQ: Meta DS guide](https://www.interviewquery.com/guides/meta-data-scientist), [HI: Meta questions](https://www.hellointerview.com/community/questions/company/Meta), [LeetCode Meta tag](https://leetcode.com/company/facebook/) (browser, Premium; the slug is still `facebook`).

### Amazon (reference)
- **Usually reported:** a strong behavioral part based on the Leadership Principles in almost every round, plus SQL or Python, statistics, and ML breadth and depth (more for applied scientist roles). Prepare several STAR stories.
- Links: [IQ: Amazon DS guide](https://www.interviewquery.com/guides/amazon-data-scientist), [DataLemur: Amazon SQL questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/amazon-sql-interview-questions), [HI: Amazon questions](https://www.hellointerview.com/community/questions/company/Amazon), [LeetCode Amazon tag](https://leetcode.com/company/amazon/) (browser, Premium).

### For every company
- Behavioral: the free [HI behavioral course](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/behavioral) (STAR stories, levelling).
- Free company-wise LeetCode lists with frequency: [liquidslr/leetcode-company-wise-problems](https://github.com/liquidslr/leetcode-company-wise-problems) (one folder per company, CSVs for 30 days, 3 months, 6 months and all time).

sections.title: Coding practice: HI, LeetCode lists, Grind 75, NeetCode
sections.summary: Pattern guides for when a pattern is weak, and curated lists for extra practice.
sections.body:
### How these fit the plan
The plan already gives you 3 problems a day from 3 different patterns. Use the pages below in two ways:
- **Explain a pattern again.** If the handbook section did not click, read the HI page for the same pattern. It explains the idea in a different way, with visuals.
- **Extra practice for one weak pattern.** Pick 2 or 3 problems of that pattern from NeetCode 150 or Grind 75. Do not start a full list from the beginning.

### HI pattern pages (free to read)
Login only adds progress tracking. Premium adds interactive visuals and guided practice.

| Handbook section | HI page |
|---|---|
| [Two pointers](#algo-two-pointers) | [Two pointers](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/two-pointers/overview) |
| [Sliding window](#algo-sliding-window) | [Fixed length](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/sliding-window/fixed-length), [variable length](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/sliding-window/variable-length) |
| [Sorting and intervals](#algo-sorting-intervals) | [Intervals](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/intervals/overview) |
| [Stack](#algo-stack) | [Stack](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/stack/overview) |
| [Monotonic stack](#algo-monotonic-stack) | [Monotonic stack](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/stack/monotonic-stack) |
| [Linked list](#algo-linked-list) | [Linked list](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/linked-list/overview) |
| [Binary search](#algo-binary-search) | [Binary search](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/binary-search/overview) |
| [Heap](#algo-heap) | [Heap](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/heap/overview) |
| [Trees](#algo-trees) | [Tree DFS](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/depth-first-search/introduction) |
| [BFS and DFS](#algo-graphs-bfs-dfs) | [Grid DFS](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/depth-first-search/matrices), [BFS](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/breadth-first-search/introduction), [multi-source BFS](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/breadth-first-search/rotting-oranges) |
| [Grid simulation](#algo-grid-simulation) | [Spiral matrix](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/matrices/spiral-matrix) |
| [Topological sort](#algo-topological-sort) | [Topological sort](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/graphs/topological-sort) |
| [Shortest path](#algo-shortest-path) | [Shortest path algorithms](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/graphs/shortest-path-algorithms) |
| [Backtracking](#algo-backtracking) | [Backtracking](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/backtracking/overview) |
| [1-D DP](#algo-dp-1d), [2-D DP](#algo-dp-2d) | [DP fundamentals](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/dynamic-programming/fundamentals) |
| [Greedy](#algo-greedy) | [Greedy](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/greedy/overview) |
| [Prefix sum](#algo-prefix-sum) | [Prefix sum](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/prefix-sum/overview) |
| (no own section) | [Trie](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code/trie/overview) |

The [index of all chapters](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/code) is a good checklist: you should know a template for each one.

### Curated lists
| List | Size and cost | Best use |
|---|---|---|
| [Grind 75](https://www.techinterviewhandbook.org/grind75/) | 75 or more problems, free | You choose weeks and hours per week and it builds a schedule. Good for picking extra problems by pattern |
| [NeetCode 150](https://neetcode.io/practice) | 150 problems, free list and videos | Video solutions when a written solution does not help |
| [NeetCode roadmap](https://neetcode.io/roadmap) | Free | Shows which pattern depends on which. Use it to order your weak areas |
| [Blind 75 (NeetCode version)](https://neetcode.io/practice/practice/blind75) | 75 problems, free | Short classic list. Many overlap with this plan |
| [LeetCode 75](https://leetcode.com/studyplan/leetcode-75/) | 75 problems, free (browser) | Core set for 2 to 3 weeks |
| [Top Exam 150](https://leetcode.com/studyplan/top-interview-150/) | 150 problems, free (browser) | Broad coverage, if you have time after the plan |
| [30 Days of Pandas](https://leetcode.com/studyplan/30-days-of-pandas/) | Free (browser) | Pandas versions of SQL questions, useful for DS take-homes. See [pandas equivalents](#sql-pandas-equivalents) |
| [Introduction to Pandas](https://leetcode.com/studyplan/introduction-to-pandas/) | Free (browser) | Warm-up for pandas syntax |

Background and origin of these lists: [TIH: best practice questions](https://www.techinterviewhandbook.org/best-practice-questions/) and the [original Blind 75 post](https://www.teamblind.com/post/New-Year-Gift---Curated-List-of-Top-75-LeetCode-Questions-to-Save-Your-Time-OaM1orEU).

### Company tags without Premium
LeetCode company tags show frequency only with Premium. Free GitHub exports of the same data:
- [liquidslr/leetcode-company-wise-problems](https://github.com/liquidslr/leetcode-company-wise-problems): updated in Aug 2026, CSVs per company and time window, with frequency. The [frequent problems table](#resources-frequent-problems) was built from it.
- [snehasishroy/leetcode-companywise-exam-questions](https://github.com/snehasishroy/leetcode-companywise-interview-questions): similar, updated in Aug 2026.
- [krishnadey30/LeetCode-Questions-CompanyWise](https://github.com/krishnadey30/LeetCode-Questions-CompanyWise): older (2024) but includes problem IDs.
- [hxu296/leetcode-company-wise-problems-2022](https://github.com/hxu296/leetcode-company-wise-problems-2022): a 2022 snapshot.

### Helpers during practice
- [AlgoMonster flowchart](https://algo.monster/flowchart): a "which pattern?" decision tree. Compare it with the [pattern recognition guide](#algo-recognize).
- [TIH: coding cheatsheet](https://www.techinterviewhandbook.org/coding-interview-cheatsheet/): what to say before, during and after coding.
- Python references: [collections](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.html), [heapq](https://docs.python.org/3/library/heapq.html), [bisect](https://docs.python.org/3/library/bisect.html), [time complexity of built-ins](https://wiki.python.org/moin/TimeComplexity). See also the [Python cheat sheet](#cheat-python).

sections.title: Frequent problems at TikTok, ByteDance, Samsung, Google (plus Meta, Amazon)
sections.summary: The most frequent company-tagged LeetCode problems, and which ones this plan already covers.
sections.body:
### Where this table comes from
- **Source:** [liquidslr/leetcode-company-wise-problems](https://github.com/liquidslr/leetcode-company-wise-problems), the "All" CSV of each company (the 6-month CSV for Google), downloaded on 2026-10-07.
- **Selection:** the top 30 TikTok problems, the top 20 Google problems from the last 6 months, the top 12 Samsung and the top 10 ByteDance problems by frequency, plus 17 high-frequency Google, Meta and Amazon staples. Two trivial or SQL items were removed.
- **Companies column:** the rank by frequency in that company's list. Google, Meta and Amazon appear only if the problem is in their top 150. TikTok, ByteDance and Samsung appear whenever the problem is tagged.
- **Small samples:** Samsung has only 62 tagged problems and ByteDance 63, so their ranks are noisy. The Samsung rows are LeetCode tags (mostly Samsung R&D India), not the Korean SW Competency Test. For that test see [Companies](#resources-companies).
- **Pattern column:** a label added by hand. The pattern name is a spoiler, so cover it if you want to practise recognition.
- **In this plan:** **Day N** means the problem is already one of that day's algorithm exam questions, with the matching handbook section. "extra" means it is not in the plan.

### How to use it
1. Do not do the extra problems before you have met their pattern in the plan.
2. Days 21 to 28: add 1 or 2 extra problems per day from this table, for your target company first.
3. When you finish one, check its pattern in the handbook and note in the mistake log if you did not see the pattern quickly.

34 of the 73 problems are already in the daily exams.

**Suggested priority if time is short** (tagged by 4 or more companies):
- Already in the plan: [LRU Cache](https://leetcode.com/problems/lru-cache/), [Number of Islands](https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-islands/), [Longest Increasing Subsequence](https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-increasing-subsequence/), [Merge Intervals](https://leetcode.com/problems/merge-intervals/), [Trapping Rain Water](https://leetcode.com/problems/trapping-rain-water/), [Course Schedule](https://leetcode.com/problems/course-schedule/), [Search in Rotated Sorted Array](https://leetcode.com/problems/search-in-rotated-sorted-array/), [Subarray Sum Equals K](https://leetcode.com/problems/subarray-sum-equals-k/), [Top K Frequent Elements](https://leetcode.com/problems/top-k-frequent-elements/), [Merge k Sorted Lists](https://leetcode.com/problems/merge-k-sorted-lists/), [Two Sum](https://leetcode.com/problems/two-sum/), [Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock](https://leetcode.com/problems/best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock/), [Valid Parentheses](https://leetcode.com/problems/valid-parentheses/), [3Sum](https://leetcode.com/problems/3sum/), [Coin Change](https://leetcode.com/problems/coin-change/), [Spiral Matrix](https://leetcode.com/problems/spiral-matrix/), [Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters](https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-substring-without-repeating-characters/).

sections.title: SQL practice sites (free and paid)
sections.summary: Where to get extra SQL questions, which parts are free, and which references to keep open.
sections.body:
### How to use them with the plan
The SQL notebooks give you 5 queries a day on Chinook, Northwind and small exam tables. Add outside SQL only when the mistake log shows the same topic twice, or in the last 10 days for company-style questions. Before each question, use the 4-step approach in [How to approach a SQL question](#sql-exam-approach).

### Practice sites
| Site | Cost | Best use |
|---|---|---|
| [DataLemur question bank](https://datalemur.com/questions) | Mostly free; some questions and solutions are Premium | Real FAANG-style SQL. Filter by company (TikTok, Google, Meta, Amazon) in the page |
| [DataLemur SQL tutorial](https://datalemur.com/sql-tutorial) | Free | Interactive refresh, up to window functions |
| [LeetCode SQL 50](https://leetcode.com/studyplan/top-sql-50/) | Free (browser) | 50 graded problems. Good on days with spare time |
| [StrataScratch](https://www.stratascratch.com/) and its [coding platform](https://platform.stratascratch.com/coding) | Free tier with a subset of questions and solutions; full access is paid; login needed to run code | Large bank tagged by company, with SQL and pandas versions |
| [SQLBolt](https://sqlbolt.com/) | Free | Quick interactive basics |
| [SQL Practice](https://www.sql-practice.com/) | Free | In-browser exercises on a hospital database |
| [Mode / ThoughtSpot SQL tutorial](https://mode.com/sql-tutorial/) | Free | Classic tutorial. It now redirects to [ThoughtSpot](https://www.thoughtspot.com/sql-tutorial). Good page on [window functions](https://www.thoughtspot.com/sql-tutorial/sql-window-functions) |

### Company question lists (free)
- [TikTok SQL questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/tiktok-sql-interview-questions)
- [Google SQL questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/google-sql-interview-questions)
- [Samsung SQL questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/samsung-sql-interview-questions)
- [Meta SQL questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/facebook-sql-interview-questions)
- [Amazon SQL questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/amazon-sql-interview-questions)

### Free versus paid: what you really need
Free material is enough for this plan: the daily notebooks, DataLemur free questions, the company blog lists and LeetCode SQL 50. A paid plan (DataLemur Premium or StrataScratch) is useful only if you want many more company-tagged questions with solutions in the last two weeks. It is not required.

### References to keep open
- [SQLite window functions](https://www.sqlite.org/windowfunctions.html): the engine used in the notebooks (`chinook.sqlite`, `northwind.db`).
- [PostgreSQL window functions](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-window.html): many exam platforms use PostgreSQL syntax.
- [pandas versus SQL](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/getting_started/comparison/comparison_with_sql.html): for take-homes in Python. See [pandas equivalents](#sql-pandas-equivalents).
- Handbook: [Window ranking](#sql-window-ranking), [Retention](#sql-retention), [Funnels](#sql-funnels) and the [SQL cheat sheet](#cheat-sql).

sections.title: Statistics, A/B testing and product sense
sections.summary: The references that examiners themselves use for experiments, metrics and product cases.
sections.body:
### Core A/B testing references
| Resource | Why it is useful |
|---|---|
| [Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments](https://experimentguide.com/) (Kohavi, Tang, Xu) | *The* A/B testing book, used at Google, Microsoft and LinkedIn. The book is paid; the site lists the chapters. Many exam questions on pitfalls come from it |
| [ExP Platform](https://exp-platform.com/) | Free papers and talks by the same authors: pitfalls, sample ratio mismatch (SRM), Twyman's law, metrics |
| [Microsoft ExP research group](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/experimentation-platform-exp/) | Free articles. Example: [checks during an experiment](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/articles/patterns-of-trustworthy-experimentation-during-experiment-stage/) (SRM and others) |
| [Udacity A/B Testing](https://www.udacity.com/course/ab-testing--ud257) | Free course by Google data scientists: metric choice, sanity checks, sizing |
| [How Not To Run an A/B Test](https://www.evanmiller.org/how-not-to-run-an-ab-test.html) | The peeking problem. A very common exam question |
| [Simple sequential A/B testing](https://www.evanmiller.org/sequential-ab-testing.html) | A good follow-up answer to "how can you stop early?" |
| [Evan Miller's A/B tools](https://www.evanmiller.org/ab-testing/) | [Sample size calculator](https://www.evanmiller.org/ab-testing/sample-size.html), [chi-squared test](https://www.evanmiller.org/ab-testing/chi-squared.html), [t-test](https://www.evanmiller.org/ab-testing/t-test.html). Use them to check your own power calculations |

Handbook links: [Power and MDE](#stats-power-mde), [A/B design](#stats-ab-design), [A/B analysis](#stats-ab-analysis), [A/B pitfalls](#stats-ab-pitfalls), [Bayesian and sequential testing](#stats-bayesian-sequential), [A/B cheat sheet](#cheat-ab-testing).

### Statistics foundations
- [Seeing Theory](https://seeing-theory.brown.edu/): visual probability, distributions, CLT, inference and regression. Good when a concept needs a picture.
- [StatQuest](https://statquest.org/video-index/) ([YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@statquest)): short videos on p-values, power, regression and trees.
- [OpenIntro Statistics](https://www.openintro.org/book/os/): free textbook for inference, proportions and regression.
- [Think Stats 3e](https://greenteapress.com/wp/think-stats-3e/): free, statistics in Python and pandas.
- Python references: [scipy.stats](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/stats.html) and [statsmodels stats](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/stats.html) (power, [z-test for proportions](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/generated/statsmodels.stats.proportion.proportions_ztest.html)).

### Question banks
- [DataLemur: 50 A/B testing questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/ab-testing-interview-questions-and-answers): duration, pitfalls, randomization, novelty, network effects.
- [DataLemur: statistics questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/statistics-interview-questions-data-science).
- [IQ: top DS questions](https://www.interviewquery.com/p/data-science-interview-questions).
- [alexeygrigorev/data-science-exams](https://github.com/alexeygrigorev/data-science-interviews): free theory Q&A on statistics and ML.

### Product sense and metric cases
- [DataLemur: product-sense questions](https://datalemur.com/blog/product-sense-interview-questions): metric definition, metric drops, trade-offs.
- [IQ: product DS questions](https://www.interviewquery.com/p/product-data-science-interview): product and metric cases.
- [IQ: A/B answer framework](https://www.interviewquery.com/p/how-to-answer-ab-testing-interview-questions): a free 6-step template.
- [DataLemur: Meta DS exam guide](https://datalemur.com/blog/meta-data-scientist-interview-guide): the clearest public description of analytical execution and analytical reasoning rounds.
- [Ace the DS book](https://www.acethedatascienceinterview.com/): book site (the book is paid). DataLemur is its free companion.

Handbook links: [Case framework](#stats-case-framework), [Product metrics](#stats-product-metrics), [Metric drop](#stats-metric-drop), [Launch decisions](#stats-launch-decisions), [Network effects](#stats-network-effects).

### Suggested order if time is short
1. "How Not To Run an A/B Test" (peeking).
2. The Microsoft ExP article on checks during an experiment (SRM).
3. DataLemur product-sense questions: answer 3 out loud with the [case framework](#stats-case-framework).
4. DataLemur 50 A/B questions: answer 10 out loud.

sections.title: Machine learning, deep learning and LLMs
sections.summary: Books, courses and ML system design guides, ordered by how fast they help in an exam.
sections.body:
### Fast exam references
| Resource | Why it is useful |
|---|---|
| [Chip Huyen: Chip Huyen's ML book](https://huyenchip.com/ml-interviews-book/) | Free. Exam process and about 200 knowledge questions. [Math chapter](https://huyenchip.com/ml-interviews-book/contents/chapter-5.-math.html) |
| [Google ML Crash Course](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course) | Free. Regression, [classification metrics](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification), embeddings, LLM intro |
| [Google: Rules of ML](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml) | 43 practical rules. Many make strong sentences in ML system design answers |
| [Google: Recommendation systems course](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/recommendation) | Candidate generation, scoring, re-ranking. Very relevant for TikTok |
| [scikit-learn user guide](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/user_guide.html) | API and concepts. [Metrics page](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html) |
| [youssefHosni DS Q&A](https://github.com/youssefHosni/Data-Science-Interview-Questions-Answers) | Free statistics, ML and deep learning Q&A |

### ML system design (HI, free "in a hurry" guide)
Start with the first two pages. They give the answer structure that the [ML system design](#ai-ml-system-design) section uses.
1. [Introduction](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/ml-system-design/in-a-hurry/introduction): what these exams test and how they are scored.
2. [Delivery](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/ml-system-design/in-a-hurry/delivery): problem, data, features, model, evaluation, serving.
3. Core concepts: [feature engineering](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/ml-system-design/core-concepts/feature-engineering), [embeddings](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/ml-system-design/core-concepts/embeddings), [generalization](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/ml-system-design/core-concepts/generalization), [evaluation](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/ml-system-design/core-concepts/evaluation) (offline metrics versus online A/B tests, the bridge to statistics).
4. Worked problems that match this plan's cases:

| Plan day | Case | HI breakdown |
|---|---|---|
| Day 24 | Feed ranking | [Video recommendations](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/ml-system-design/problem-breakdowns/video-recommendations) |
| Day 25 | Content moderation / integrity | [Harmful content](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/ml-system-design/problem-breakdowns/harmful-content), [bot detection](https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/ml-system-design/problem-breakdowns/bot-detection) (imbalanced labels) |

More MLSD question collections: [khangich/machine-learning-exam](https://github.com/khangich/machine-learning-interview) and [alirezadir/Machine-Learning-Exams](https://github.com/alirezadir/Machine-Learning-Interviews) (now redirects to a renamed repo).

### Deep learning and transformers
- [Jay Alammar: The Illustrated Transformer](https://jalammar.github.io/illustrated-transformer/): the standard visual explanation of attention. Read before [Attention and transformers](#ai-attention-transformer).
- Jay Alammar on [GPT-2](https://jalammar.github.io/illustrated-gpt2/), [BERT](https://jalammar.github.io/illustrated-bert/) and [word2vec](https://jalammar.github.io/illustrated-word2vec/): decoder-only models, pretraining and fine-tuning, embeddings.
- [3Blue1Brown: neural networks](https://www.3blue1brown.com/topics/neural-networks): visual intuition for backpropagation and transformers.
- [Andrej Karpathy: Neural Networks Zero to Hero](https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html): free video course from micrograd to GPT. Single videos: [Let's build GPT](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kCc8FmEb1nY), [Intro to LLMs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zjkBMFhNj_g), [Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7xTGNNLPyMI), [backprop with micrograd](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VMj-3S1tku0), [Let's reproduce GPT-2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l8pRSuU81PU). All on his [YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@AndrejKarpathy).
- [Hugging Face LLM course](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter1/1): transformers, tokenizers, fine-tuning. [All courses](https://huggingface.co/learn).

### LLM applications
- [Chip Huyen: Building LLM applications for production](https://huyenchip.com/2023/04/11/llm-engineering.html): prompting versus fine-tuning, evaluation, cost and latency. Matches [RAG](#ai-rag), [LLM evaluation](#ai-llm-evaluation) and [Safety and cost](#ai-safety-cost).
- [Lilian Weng: Lil'Log](https://lilianweng.github.io/): deep surveys on [attention](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2018-06-24-attention/), the [transformer family](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2023-01-27-the-transformer-family-v2/), [LLM agents](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2023-06-23-agent/), [large-model training](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2021-09-25-train-large/) and [reward hacking](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2024-11-28-reward-hacking/). Related: [Agents](#ai-agents), [Fine-tuning and RLHF](#ai-fine-tuning-rlhf).

### Textbooks and courses (deep reference, not for the last week)
| Resource | Notes |
|---|---|
| [An Introduction to Statistical Learning](https://www.statlearning.com/) | Free PDF. The best single classic ML and statistics book for DS |
| [Elements of Statistical Learning](https://hastie.su.domains/ElemStatLearn/) | Free PDF. Advanced |
| [Stanford CS229](https://cs229.stanford.edu/) | Classic ML math. [Main notes PDF](https://cs229.stanford.edu/main_notes.pdf) |
| [Deep Learning Book](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/) | Free online |
| [Dive into Deep Learning](https://d2l.ai/) | Free, with runnable PyTorch code |
| [Stanford CME 295](https://cme295.stanford.edu/) | Compact course on transformers and LLMs |
| [Stanford CS336](https://stanford-cs336.github.io/) | Language models from scratch. Only if time allows |

### Suggested order if time is short
1. HI MLSD introduction and delivery pages, then the video recommendations breakdown.
2. The Illustrated Transformer.
3. Chip Huyen on LLM applications.
4. Google Rules of ML: skim the rule titles.

sections.title: Datasets used in the notebooks
sections.summary: The real datasets in exam_prep/data, where they come from, and their license.
sections.body:
All files are in `exam_prep/data/`. Each one was downloaded from the source below and loaded with pandas or sqlite3 on 2026-10-07. Every source is a direct download with no login, so the notebooks can download a missing file in Colab. Labels used below: **SQL** = joins, windows, aggregation; **Stats**; **A/B** = experiment analysis; **ML**; **NLP** = text classification.

### Product and user-behaviour data
| File | Content | Source | License / terms | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cookie_cats.csv` | Real mobile-game A/B test, 90,189 players. `version` (gate_30 = control, gate_40 = treatment), `sum_gamerounds`, `retention_1`, `retention_7` | [GitHub mirror](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robguilarr/ab_testing_cookie_cats/main/datasets/cookie_cats.csv) ([second mirror](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/basilghauri/A-B-Testing-of-Mobile-Game/main/cookie_cats.csv)); originally from a DataCamp project | No license in the mirror: educational use only | A/B (two-proportion test, bootstrap, heavy-tailed metric), Stats |
| `ab_data.csv` | 294,478 rows: `user_id`, `timestamp`, `group`, `landing_page`, `converted`. Has deliberate mismatches and duplicate users | [GitHub mirror](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/F-Zarian/Analyze_AB_test_results/main/ab_data.csv) of a Udacity project | No license in the mirror: educational use only | A/B (data checks, SRM, z-test, logistic regression), SQL |
| `ab_countries.csv` | `user_id`, `country` (UK/US/CA). Join to `ab_data` | [GitHub mirror](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/F-Zarian/Analyze_AB_test_results/main/countries.csv) | Same as above | Segment effects, SQL joins |
| `telco_churn.csv` | 7,043 customers: demographics, services, contract, charges, `Churn` | [IBM sample data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IBM/telco-customer-churn-on-icp4d/master/data/Telco-Customer-Churn.csv) | Apache-2.0 | ML (churn, imbalance, metrics), product sense |
| `googleplaystore.csv` | 10,841 apps: category, rating, reviews, installs, price. Messy strings | [GitHub mirror](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malborroni/Foundations_of_Computer-Science/master/datasets/googleplaystore.csv) of a Kaggle dataset | No license in the mirror: study use only | Data cleaning, Stats, SQL |
| `googleplaystore_user_reviews.csv` | 64,295 reviews with sentiment labels (many NaN) | [GitHub mirror](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malborroni/Foundations_of_Computer-Science/master/datasets/googleplaystore_user_reviews.csv) | Same as above | NLP (sentiment) |
| `movielens_*.csv` (ratings, movies, tags, links) | 100,836 ratings by users on 9,742 movies | [GroupLens ml-latest-small.zip](https://files.grouplens.org/datasets/movielens/ml-latest-small.zip) | GroupLens license: research and education, acknowledge it, no commercial use without permission | ML (recommenders), SQL (windows, cohorts) |
| `online_retail.csv.gz` | 541,909 invoice lines of a UK online shop, 2010-12 to 2011-12. A "C" prefix on `InvoiceNo` means a cancellation | [UCI Online Retail](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/352/online+retail.zip) (converted locally from xlsx) | CC BY 4.0 | SQL (RFM, cohorts, retention), segmentation |
| `bank_marketing.csv` (`sep=";"`) | 41,188 calls of a bank campaign, target `y` (about 11% yes). `duration` leaks the target | [UCI Bank Marketing](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/222/bank+marketing.zip) | CC BY 4.0 | ML (imbalance, leakage) |
| `sms_spam.tsv` | 5,572 SMS messages, about 13% spam | [UCI SMS Spam Collection](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/228/sms+spam+collection.zip) | CC BY 4.0 | NLP (TF-IDF, precision and recall) |

### SQL databases
| File | Content | Source | License | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chinook.sqlite` | Digital music store: 11 tables (customers, invoices, tracks, employees with a manager column) | [lerocha/chinook-database release](https://github.com/lerocha/chinook-database/releases/download/v1.4.5/Chinook_Sqlite.sqlite) | MIT-style | Joins, revenue by group, top-N per group, self-joins |
| `northwind.db` | Orders database with 16,282 orders and 609,283 order lines (quote `"Order Details"`) | [jpwhite3/northwind-SQLite3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpwhite3/northwind-SQLite3/main/dist/northwind.db) | MIT | Window functions, growth, retention, baskets |
| `jaffle_raw_*.csv` (customers, orders, payments) | 100 customers, 99 orders, 113 payments (amounts in cents) | [dbt-labs/jaffle_shop seeds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dbt-labs/jaffle_shop/main/seeds/raw_customers.csv) (same folder for `raw_orders.csv` and `raw_payments.csv`) | Apache-2.0 | Small SQL warm-ups you can check by hand |

### Classic small tables (seaborn-data)
`tips.csv`, `penguins.csv`, `titanic.csv`, `taxis.csv`, `diamonds.csv`, `flights.csv`, `mpg.csv`. Source pattern: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwaskom/seaborn-data/master/<name>.csv`. There is no license file; the repo is meant for the seaborn documentation and files may change. Use them for study only.

| File | Rows | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `tips.csv` | 244 | t-tests, regression, confidence intervals |
| `penguins.csv` | 344 | Classification, clustering, ANOVA, missing data |
| `titanic.csv` | 891 | Logistic regression, trees, chi-square |
| `taxis.csv` | 6,433 | Marketplace metrics, time functions, regression |
| `diamonds.csv` | 53,940 | Regression, log transforms, feature engineering |
| `flights.csv` | 144 | Time series, window functions |
| `mpg.csv` | 398 | Regression, correlation, missing values |

### Caveats
- The A/B files and the Google Play files come from personal GitHub mirrors with no license, so they could disappear. A second mirror is listed for `cookie_cats.csv`. The originals on DataCamp and Kaggle need a login.
- `online_retail.csv.gz` was converted from the UCI xlsx file. Its source URL is a zip with an xlsx inside, so an automatic download does not give the same file. See [Colab setup](#resources-colab).
- Datasets with "study use only" terms are fine for private practice. Do not republish them.

sections.title: Colab setup
sections.summary: Open the notebooks in Google Colab straight from GitHub, nothing to upload.
sections.body:
### Open a notebook
- Use the links in the [Plan](#plan) tab, or start with [00_start_here](https://colab.research.google.com/github/mahsa-agz/mahsa-agz.github.io/blob/main/ds-handbook/exam_prep/00_start_here.ipynb): it lists every day with one link per notebook.
- Each notebook also has an **Open in Colab** button at the top, and its last cell links the next notebook of the day.
- Everything lives in one public repository: [https://github.com/mahsa-agz/mahsa-agz.github.io/tree/main/ds-handbook](https://github.com/mahsa-agz/mahsa-agz.github.io/tree/main/ds-handbook).

### The first cell (setup)
Run the **Setup** cell before anything else. It defines the helpers (`check()` for algorithms, `run()` for SQL) and
downloads the data files the notebook needs from the repository into Colab. No Google Drive access is needed.

### Keep your answers
A notebook opened from GitHub is a temporary copy. To keep your work, use **File > Save a copy in Drive** in Colab
before you start typing; then always open your saved copy for that day.

### If something does not work
| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| A data download fails | Run the Setup cell again; check your internet connection. |
| `NameError` for `check`, `run` or `data_path` | Run the Setup cell first (after every Colab restart too). |
| A package is missing | Run `%pip install <name>` in a new cell, then run the Setup cell again. |
| Colab disconnected after a long break | **Runtime > Run all** brings everything back; your saved copy keeps your code. |
